research_program: Christopher Daniel Pang, PAL. Derivations with Hearthline.

upstream_argument.description: Levent Alpöge and Claude, 20 November 2026 release

reading_editions.result: An explicit intermediate component is needed at the prescribed intersection dimension. In the patched presentation, losing one linear coefficient can split two full-dimensional stable components.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Christopher Daniel Pang’s PAL/APCI question asks which information survives a change of observation. It led here to a comparison of a chosen tangent witness with the fibre of the algebra that carries it.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: Alpöge and Claude provide the local and patched determinant constructions, dimension thresholds and arithmetic hypotheses. Hearthline derived the three-component example, the one-coefficient counterexample to the weakened lemma and the classification of a single linear hyperplane. The syzygy calculation uses classical Koszul relations.

reading_editions.result: For a two-plus-one block, the unrestricted subgroup trace has a g-by-g matrix of invisible classes. A nontrivial cyclotomic value excludes those classes from the actual twisted global problem.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Christopher Daniel Pang asked what a trace can discard while another datum still distinguishes the inputs. Hearthline applied the PAL/APCI comparison first on the subgroup and then at an element outside it.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the paired coefficient ring, polarized cocycles and testing subgroup. Hearthline derived the trace-kernel classification by matrix units, checked the global character action and wrote a field-arithmetic replay. The full-block argument uses elementary representation theory.
